prompt:
SQL Server 2019, compat level 150. Following advice I created this index:

CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Tickets_Assignee_Created ON dbo.Tickets (AssigneeId, CreatedAt, Priority);

Query (runs ~300/min from the helpdesk app):
SELECT TOP (20) TicketId, Subject, Priority, CreatedAt
FROM dbo.Tickets
WHERE AssigneeId = @AssigneeId AND CreatedAt >= @Since
ORDER BY Priority DESC, CreatedAt DESC;

Tickets has 18M rows, clustered PK on TicketId. A busy agent has ~400k tickets, about 40k of them since @Since (usually 30 days ago). Subject is nvarchar(400).

Here's the actual execution plan summary I got (STATISTICS IO/TIME + actual plan):
- Top (20 rows)
- Sort (Priority DESC, CreatedAt DESC) — Actual rows 41,233 — warning: Operator used tempdb to spill data during execution with spill level 1
- Nested Loops (Inner Join)
  - Index Seek IX_Tickets_Assignee_Created, Seek Predicate: AssigneeId = @AssigneeId AND CreatedAt >= @Since, Actual rows 41,233, Estimated rows 1,850
  - Key Lookup (Clustered) PK_Tickets, executions 41,233
Table 'Tickets'. Scan count 1, logical reads 131,904
CPU time = 312 ms, elapsed time = 655 ms.

Still slow. What's wrong and what should I do next?
assertions: The response identifies that the Sort/tempdb spill happens because the index order (AssigneeId, CreatedAt, ...) does not match ORDER BY Priority DESC, CreatedAt DESC (range column before sort column)
The response recommends an index keyed (AssigneeId, Priority DESC, CreatedAt DESC) or equivalent ESR order
The response recommends INCLUDE (Subject) (or otherwise making the index covering) to remove the Key Lookup
The response points out the estimated 1,850 vs actual 41,233 rows gap and links it to statistics and/or parameter sniffing
The response estimates or reasons about how many rows the new index will read for TOP 20 given ~10% of the agent's tickets match @Since
The response says what to do with the existing IX_Tickets_Assignee_Created (replace/drop after verification, or DROP_EXISTING)
The response mentions building online (ONLINE = ON) and/or its edition requirement
The response asks for a new actual execution plan and STATISTICS IO to compare logical reads before and after
